info.name: NyayMitra API
info.description:
NyayMitra backend API collection — working requests for every endpoint the team tests against.

BASE URL: {{baseUrl}} (http://localhost:8000)

AUTHENTICATION
- One login endpoint for every role: POST /api/auth/login.
- Register: POST /api/auth/register creates a USER; POST /api/auth/register/lawyer creates a LAWYER (lands PENDING verification — only an admin can approve).
- The register and login requests below save the returned token to the collection variable `token` automatically. Run one of them before any protected request. Run the Admin Login before the /api/admin/* requests.
- Protected routes: Authorization: Bearer {{token}}.
- Logout (POST /api/auth/logout) revokes the current token.

LAWYER VERIFICATION (ADMIN only)
- verification_status vocabulary is exactly: PENDING, APPROVED, REJECTED.
- GET /api/admin/lawyers — list registrations (?status=PENDING is the approvals queue, page/limit paging).
- GET /api/admin/lawyers/{lawyer_id} — one registration in full.
- PATCH /api/admin/lawyers/{lawyer_id} — body {"verification_status": "APPROVED" | "REJECTED" | "PENDING"}.
- A lawyer (or any non-ADMIN token) receives 403 on every /api/admin/* route — self-approval is impossible.

VERIFICATION DOCUMENTS (lawyer registration, part 2)
- POST /api/auth/lawyer/verification-document - multipart/form-data (field 'file'), LAWYER token, PDF/JPG/PNG, max 10 MB; re-upload replaces the previous copy; 409 once APPROVED.
- GET /api/auth/lawyer/verification-document - the caller's own file bytes (attachment).
- GET /api/admin/lawyers/{lawyer_id}/document - ADMIN-only file bytes (attachment); 404 when nothing was uploaded.
- No static file route exists - uploads live outside any web root, one server-generated file per lawyer.

DEMO ACCOUNTS (seeded for integration testing only — see README "Demo credentials")
- USER:   asha@example.com / user123
- LAWYER: rohan@example.com / lawyer123 (APPROVED)
- ADMIN:  admin@nyaymitra.in / admin123

ERRORS: validation 400/422, bad credentials 401 (generic), wrong role 403, duplicates 409, unknown id 404 — always {"detail": "..."}.

CHAT (Phase 3)
- Folder 'Chat (User ↔ Lawyer)': directory of APPROVED lawyers, get-or-create conversations from either side, history and sending — all bearer-authenticated via the same {{token}} as the other folders.
- Set {{token}} from any Login response, then follow the folder order (user side, then lawyer side).

item.name: Authentication
item.description: One system for every role. The register and login requests store the access token in `token` automatically.

request.description: 201 → signed in as role USER. The server assigns the role; sending "role" in the body is rejected with 422. Passwords are stored only as PBKDF2 hashes.

body.raw:
{
  "full_name": "Test Advocate",
  "email": "test.advocate@example.com",
  "password": "change-me-123",
  "password_confirmation": "change-me-123",
  "license_id": "ENR/TEST/0001",
  "practice_areas": [
    "Criminal Law",
    "Family Law"
  ],
  "bar_council": "Bar Council of Maharashtra",
  "years_of_experience": 7,
  "professional_phone_number": "+91 98765 43210",
  "professional_bio": "High Court advocate, 7 years of practice."
}

request.description: 201 -> signed in as role LAWYER with verification_status = PENDING. license_id is required and unique; practice_areas is a string array (1-10 items, de-duplicated server-side). Optional profile fields: bar_council (<=200 chars), years_of_experience (0-70), professional_phone_number (5-50 chars of digits/space/+/()-), professional_bio (<=1000 chars) -> 400 when out of bounds. The client cannot send verification_status, role or lawyer_id - those fields are rejected with 422 (self-approval at the door is impossible). PART 1 of the submission: follow with 'Upload Verification Document' using the token saved below.

formdata.description: PDF, JPG or PNG, max 10 MB (magic bytes, extension and content-type must agree).

request.description: PART 2 of lawyer registration: attach the licence/registration document (multipart/form-data, field name 'file'). Needs the LAWYER token saved by Register Lawyer. 201 -> document metadata {filename, mime_type, size_bytes, sha256, uploaded_at}. Re-uploading REPLACES the previous copy (one lawyer, one file); allowed while PENDING or REJECTED, 409 once APPROVED. 400 for wrong type/size/empty file, 401 signed out, 403 for non-LAWYER tokens. The file is never served statically - bytes leave the server only through this lawyer's own GET /api/auth/lawyer/verification-document or the ADMIN-only GET /api/admin/lawyers/{id}/document.

The single login endpoint for USER, LAWYER and ADMIN alike. Unknown email and wrong password answer with the same 401 ("Invalid email or password."). Pre-filled with the seeded demo USER; the password is a documented demo credential, not a real one.
Seeded demo LAWYER (verification_status = APPROVED). Use /api/auth/me with this token to see verification_status and lawyer_id.
Seeded demo ADMIN — integration-testing only; there is no self-registration path for ADMIN. Run this before any /api/admin/* request: it overwrites `token` with the admin session.

The reference protected route. 401 without a valid token. Returns user_id, full_name, email, role, is_demo, lawyer_id and — for LAWYER accounts — verification_status (PENDING/APPROVED/REJECTED). Never a password hash.

The signed-in advocate's own registration: lawyer_id, license_id, practice_areas (array), verification_status, verified_at, optional profile fields (bar_council, years_of_experience, professional_phone_number, professional_bio) and document: null until a licence file is uploaded, then {filename, mime_type, size_bytes, sha256, uploaded_at} - metadata only, never the bytes (fetch those via GET /api/auth/lawyer/verification-document). Available to PENDING, APPROVED and REJECTED lawyers alike (this is the status screen). 401 signed out, 403 for non-LAWYER roles.
Revokes the presented token. 200 {"message": "Signed out."} — afterwards /me answers 401.

item.name: Admin — Lawyer Verification
item.description: ADMIN-only. Run "Login (demo ADMIN)" first so `token` holds the admin session — every route below answers 403 to any other role, including the lawyer being ruled on (self-approval is impossible).

request.description: Every lawyer registration, newest first. Envelope: {count, total_count, page, limit, total_pages, lawyers[]} — the same shape GET /api/lawyers returns, so the Admin Dashboard renders both with one type.
The approvals queue. status accepts exactly PENDING, APPROVED or REJECTED — anything else is 422.

One registration in full: name, email, license_id, practice_areas, verification_status, verified_by/verified_at, created_at, optional profile fields (bar_council, years_of_experience, professional_phone_number, professional_bio) and document metadata ({filename, mime_type, size_bytes, sha256, uploaded_at} or null when nothing was uploaded) so the dashboard can flag applications without proof. 404 'Lawyer not found' for an unknown id.

ADMIN only: the uploaded licence/registration file itself (file bytes, real content-type, Content-Disposition: attachment, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff). Run the Admin Login first so {{token}} is an ADMIN token. 401 signed out, 403 for every non-ADMIN token (including the lawyer's own), 404 'Document not found' when nothing was uploaded. The uploads directory is never served statically - this endpoint and the lawyer's own GET /api/auth/lawyer/verification-document are the only two ways bytes leave the server.
Records verified_by (the admin's user id) and verified_at, and the lawyer's own /me reads APPROVED immediately — no re-login. Sending any other field (e.g. verified_by) is 422.
The lawyer can still log in and read their own status; lawyer-only features answer 403 "Your lawyer registration has been rejected."
Clears verified_by and verified_at — "nobody has ruled" must read that way to every screen.
CNR lookup against the development dataset. 200 → the case record; unknown/malformed CNR → the service's own refusal message.

item.name: Chat (User ↔ Lawyer)
item.description: Phase 3 messaging over plain HTTP — no WebSockets. Identity always comes from the session token: request bodies never carry the sender or the thread's owner (extra fields are 422). Only APPROVED lawyers are listed or reachable; conversations are visible to their two participants only (anyone else gets 404). Demo flow: login as the demo USER → directory → start conversation → send; then login as the demo LAWYER (already APPROVED) → list → reply.

request.description: 200 {count, lawyers[]} — only verification_status=APPROVED lawyers, each with name, practice areas, experience, bio and bar council (never email, licence id or phone). PENDING/REJECTED never appear. Signed out → 401; any signed-in role may browse.

200 {count, conversations[]} — the signed-in citizen's threads only, newest activity first, each with both participants, optional case_cnr and the full message history. LAWYER or ADMIN session → 403; signed out → 401. There is no parameter that can widen the filter.

201 created / 200 reused — one thread per (citizen, lawyer) pair, never a duplicate. The lawyer must exist AND be APPROVED: unknown and unavailable ids answer identically (404 'Lawyer not found or not available for chat.') so registrations cannot be probed. case_cnr is optional (4 letters + 12 digits, stored upper-cased; malformed → 400). A user_id in the payload → 422: the owner is always the session.

200 {count, conversations[]} — threads involving the signed-in advocate only (same shape as the user list, same newest-first order). PENDING/REJECTED lawyer token → 403 with that lawyer's own status message; other roles → 403; signed out → 401.

201 created / 200 reused — a verified lawyer opens (or reuses) the thread with a client, e.g. the 'Message client' button on a case. user_id must belong to a real USER account, else 404 'Account not found.' A lawyer_id in the payload → 422: the thread is always bound to the session's own lawyer. Pending/rejected → 403.

200 ConversationOut with full history — participants only: the citizen on the thread or a verified lawyer on it. Anybody else (including a valid-but-different user/lawyer) → 404, which leaks nothing about which ids exist; unknown id → 404; non-numeric id → 422 (never a 500); ADMIN → 403; signed out → 401.

200 {count, messages[]} in send order (oldest first). sender_role ('USER'/'LAWYER') is derived from which side of the thread the sender sits on — it is not stored, so it cannot be spoofed. Same access rules as Get Conversation.

201 ChatMessageOut — sender_id is taken from the session, never from the payload (a sender_id field in the body → 422). Blank message → 400; over 4000 characters → 400; non-participant → 404; signed out → 401. Messages persist server-side across refresh and re-login.

body.raw: {"message": "Namaste, I need help with my case."}
